title: chore: Update CSpell configuration
body:
## :bookmark_tabs: Summary

> Brief description about the content of your PR.

Resolves #5176

1. Updated CSpell from v6 to v8
2. Converted `cSpell.json` to `cspell.config.yaml` for ease of use.
3. Moved the words out of `cSpell.json` and into separate dictionaries in the `./.cspell/` dir.
4. Removed most of the `ignoreRegExpList` patterns since they hid spelling issues.
5. Update `fixCSpell.ts` to sort the dictionary files: `./.cspell/*.txt`.
6. Enabled the spell checking of variable names and strings for production code.
7. Enabled the spell checking of code within Markdown files.
8. Fix spelling issues.

## :straight_ruler: Design Decisions

> Describe the way your implementation works or what design decisions you made if applicable.

Since the code base was in pretty good shape, there wasn't a lot of changes or fixes that were needed. Most of the work was adding words to the various dictionaries.

#### Dictionaries

1. `code-terms` - For code related terms like `loglevel`
2. `mermaid-terms` - For Mermaid related terms or APIs.
3. `contributors` - For the names of contributors mentioned in the code or documentation.
4. `3rd-party-terms` - For terms from third party libraries. 
5. `misc` - For things that didn't really belong in any of the above. 

There should be NO functional changes to Mermaid.

### :clipboard: Tasks

Make sure you

- [x] :book: have read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] :computer: have added necessary unit/e2e tests.
   Functionality should not have changed.
- [x] :notebook: have added documentation. Make sure [`MERMAID_RELEASE_VERSION`](https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/blob/develop/packages/mermaid/src/docs/community/contributing.md#update-documentation) is used for all new features.
- [x] :bookmark: targeted `develop` branch

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body:
:laughing:

Maybe we should add `en-GB,en-US` to specify that both American English and British English is allowed (I'm a fan of `en-GB-oxendict`, which is like a mix of American and British English spelling).
comments.label_reasoning: The comment suggests updating the CSpell configuration to explicitly specify supported English language variants, a configuration/documentation concern.

comments.author: Jason3S
comments.body:
@aloisklink,

I can change the language to `en-GB,en-US` to capture both spelling variants. Do you have a link to a hunspell `en-GB-oxendict` dictionary? I didn't find a clear source for one.

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body:
Hmmmm, maybe it's not supported by hunspell: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxford_spelling (or hunspell's `en-GB` already includes it in their dictionary). It's the variant of English used by ISO/ the UN, and most British academic journals.

It's basically `en-GB`, except most words use the `-ize` instead of `-ise`, e.g. organize vs organise. `en-GB,en-US` though should cover it completely, though!

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: The comment suggests adding `en-GB,en-US` to the CSpell configuration, implying a concrete change.

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body:
I'm a bit scared of this change.

I'm pretty sure the old text does nothing, but I don't know if the new text does anything.

Maybe we should delete it?

```suggestion
```

Or do:

```suggestion
%options easy_keword_rules // cspell: disable-line
```

It was originally `%options easy_keyword_rules` before https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/commit/6077ba54054eed165052d73fe342b6ad3bf04e8c

_Edit_: looking at https://gerhobbelt.github.io/jison/docs/#literal-tokens, it seems like `%options easy_keyword_rules` is enabled by default in `jison`, but not in some other jison implementations? Just in case, we should probably not change anything.
